title: Unified Filesystem Operations for Local and Remote Connections
text: netfs extends fs’s filesystem interface remote connections. Every function keeps fs’s names, arguments, return types; adding con = <connection> sends call FTP, SSH, SMB, WebDAV, S3 server instead local disk. Calls without con delegate directly fs.

title: Unified Filesystem Operations for Local and Remote Connections
code: install.packages(".", repos = NULL, type = "source")

title: Unified Filesystem Operations for Local and Remote Connections
text: ftp(), ssh(), smb() describe connection without contacting server; connection never prints password. Substitute one another without changing rest code: Remote paths work without leading slash:
code: library(netfs)  dir_ls("data")                                        # local, as usual  server <- ssh("server.example.org", user = "user") dir_ls("/data", con = server) file_download("/data/input.csv", local = "input.csv", con = server) server <- smb("fileserver", "DATA") dir_ls("/reports", con = server) dir_ls(server)                       # shorthand for the connection's root dir_ls("/reports", con = server) dir_ls("reports", con = server)

title: Unified Filesystem Operations for Local and Remote Connections
text: netfs_capabilities() reports engine package values, plus whether actually available current machine. SMB handled entirely smbclientr: Samba’s smbclient Linux macOS (brew install samba), native UNC access Windows. WebDAV handled entirely webdav package, built httr2 alone. S3 handled entirely s3fs, built paws alone. None three need external binary; three translate errors netfs’s condition classes otherwise stay protocol. WebDAV connection identified single base URL rather separate host port, since URL commonly carries server-specific path prefix (per-user DAV root, instance). S3 connection scoped one bucket, way smb() scoped one share - paths always relative bucket’s key namespace. Neither WebDAV S3 server-side rename, file_move() either copy followed deleting source - atomic: delete fails, copies left behind rather neither.
code: server <- webdav("https://cloud.example.org/remote.php/dav/files/alice/", user = "alice") dir_ls("/reports", con = server)  bucket <- s3("my-bucket", region_name = "us-east-1") dir_ls("/reports", con = bucket) netfs_capabilities()          # client availability, this machine netfs_capabilities(server)    # operations this connection supports

title: Unified Filesystem Operations for Local and Remote Connections
text: netfs covers fs’s full remote-relevant API: alongside dir_ls(), file_copy(), file_move(), file_info(), operations , also provides dir_info(), dir_map(), dir_walk(), dir_tree(), dir_copy(), file_size(), file_create(), is_file(), is_dir(), is_link(), is_file_empty(), is_dir_empty(), file_access(), file_chmod(), file_chown(), file_touch(), link_create(), link_path(), link_copy(), link_delete(). dir_ls() dir_info() take recurse argument. fs functions remote counterpart, never touch connection’s filesystem first place: fs::path_*() functions plain string manipulation work unchanged remote path; file_temp() group_ids()/user_ids() refer local machine. Call fs:: directly . Permissions, ownership, arbitrary timestamps, symlinks (file_chmod(), file_chown(), file_touch() explicit timestamp, file_access()’s read/write/execute modes, every link_*() function) work SSH, one backend real remote shell behind . FTP, SMB, WebDAV, S3 consistent equivalent raise netfs_unsupported. file_show() always raises , remote connection - opens local viewer, meaning path isn’t machine.

title: Unified Filesystem Operations for Local and Remote Connections
text: Server-side file_copy() isn’t available FTP, copy command protocol; fails netfs_unsupported. SSH, SMB, WebDAV, S3 support natively. dir_copy() works everywhere regardless: FTP, file copied local staging download upload. S3 atomic “fail empty” primitive way rmdir FTP’s RMD - dir_delete() without recurse = TRUE still refuses non-empty “directory” , checking extra listing first, single native call. SSH authentication never places password command line; use agent, SSH configuration, identity file. Operations one connection share single OpenSSH ControlMaster session Unix, repeated calls reuse handshake instead reconnecting time (available Windows). file_touch() explicit timestamp requires GNU touch remote; BSD/macOS SSH servers aren’t currently supported case. SMB Windows (native UNC access, via smbclientr) run successfully live server one Windows machine, still experimental - broader testing ongoing. Linux macOS, going Samba’s smbclient, better exercised. Unit tests run mocked transports don’t require live server. Remote errors inherit netfs_error, subclasses authentication, missing paths, permissions, timeouts, unavailable backends, unsupported operations.

title: netfs 0.1.0
text: Added initial local, SSH, FTP/FTPS, SMB filesystem API. Added structured errors, capability reporting, secret-safe connections. SMB client installation left operating system. Missing Unix clients now produce platform-specific setup guidance. macOS SMB operations now use separately installed Samba smbclient utility, Linux, instead mounting share natively AppleScript. Install Homebrew (brew install samba); MacPorts samba4 port known crash connect macOS versions. Fixed FTP dir_create(), dir_delete(), file_delete(), file_move() silently -op’ing instead sending commands. Fixed SMB directory listings (dir_ls()) parsing smbclient’s actual output format, listing subdirectory’s contents without explicit wildcard. Fixed issue authenticated SMB call lose PATH fail find smbclient. Fixed .run_command() occasionally reporting unrelated errors (input validation failures) generic process-execution failure. Fixed file_download()/file_upload() expanding ~ local. Raised smbclient’s default send-buffer size avoid NT_STATUS_IO_TIMEOUT slower connections large transfers; override smb(..., send_buffer = <bytes>). dir_ls() gained type argument filter remote listings entry type, matching fs::dir_ls(). Remote dir_ls(), file_info(), mutating file/dir operations now return fs-typed results (fs_path, fs_bytes, fs::file_info() compatible type factor) instead plain character/numeric values. Added concise set_creds(), get_creds(), delete_creds() keyring API. SMB support now provided smbclientr package (optional, Suggests-dependency - installed use smb()). netfs’s SMB implementation gone; smb(), set_creds()/get_creds()/ delete_creds(), every remote filesystem operation keep exact public behavior, now thin adapter translates smbclientr’s errors netfs’s condition classes. One user-visible improvement rebase: server-side file_copy() now supported SMB (via smbclient’s scopy native Windows copy), previously errored netfs_unsupported. Fixed file_exists()/file_info() FTP effectively downloading file’s entire contents just check exists (confirmed real server: 18s 22MB file, versus 4s fix - large file take minutes effectively hang). Uses curl’s nobody = TRUE (FTP SIZE/MDTM query) instead full fetch. file_info() now returns real size modification_time FTP files (previously always NA), read lightweight request. Fixed file_info() SSH breaking macOS/BSD remotes: used stat -c, GNU-coreutils-specific syntax; falls back BSD’s stat -f syntax fails. Unix, operations SSH connection now share one OpenSSH ControlMaster connection instead opening new one (full handshake authentication) per call - confirmed live: roughly 9-13x speedup repeated operations. available Windows. Added ssh_keygen(), utility generate ed25519 identity file SSH connection print ssh-copy-id command registers server. never contacts server . Fixed file_upload()/file_download() remotes modern OpenSSH client’s default SFTP transfer served process doesn’t share login shell’s view filesystem (confirmed live Windows OpenSSH Git Bash default shell: test -d/find saw path native sftp-server reported missing). scp now forced onto legacy, shell-routed protocol (-O) consistency every SSH operation. Fixed file_upload()/file_download() mangling remote paths containing spaces shell-metacharacters, fixed downloads path failing outright protocol error: filename match request. scp’s remote target never parsed shell locally, escaping - must arrive backslash-escaped remote shell, netfs’s ordinary single-quote-style shell quoting (, downloads, broke scp’s check server’s reported filename matches requested). Fixed file_info() SSH failing “SSH returned unrecognized metadata” Windows/MSYS2-packaged GNU coreutils stat (confirmed live Git Bash): printed format string’s \t escape sequence verbatim instead converting tab way Linux’s stat , netfs’s parser never found field separator. format string now embeds literal tab byte instead, every stat tested passes unchanged without needing interpret . Added rest fs’s API remote connections, backed entirely existing dir_ls()/file_info()/file_exists()/dir_exists()/ file_copy() primitives works every backend already support: dir_info(), dir_map(), dir_walk(), dir_tree(), dir_copy(), file_size(), file_create(), is_file(), is_dir(), is_link(), is_file_empty(), is_dir_empty(). dir_ls()/dir_info() also gained recurse argument. Added file_chmod(), file_chown(), file_touch(), file_access() ("read"/"write"/"execute" modes), link_create(), link_path(), link_copy(), link_delete(). POSIX permissions, ownership, arbitrary timestamps, symlinks consistent equivalent across FTP SMB, SSH-(routed remote shell via chmod/chown/touch/test -r|-w|-x/ln -s/readlink); calling one FTP SMB connection fails immediately clear netfs_unsupported error naming operation backend, rather silently -op’ing leaking generic error. file_touch() explicit (non-“now”) timestamp additionally requires GNU touch remote - BSD/macOS’s -t flag uses server’s local time, project reachable BSD SSH target verify correct conversion . Added file_show(), refused remote connection - opens path local viewer, remote path isn’t machine. Fixed file_info() SSH never recognizing symlink: GNU/BSD stat describe one form “symbolic link”, matched neither “directory” “file” branch, type silently came back NA. Fixed missing remote path SSH (e.g. file_info() one) raising generic netfs_backend_error instead netfs_not_found, unlike every backend - every coreutils tool tested reports missing target “file directory” phrase. connection every SSH operation already runs . marked unsupported outright, FTP (genuinely copy command base protocol ); SSH never needed local download/upload round-trip imply, since -server copy never leave server. dir_copy() longer fails partway (leaving incomplete destination directory behind) backend without native file_copy() - currently just FTP. file instead falls back local-staging download+upload, copy still completes. netfs_capabilities(con) now reports support every operation . Added fourth remote backend, webdav(), delegating webdav package (built httr2 alone - external binary, unlike SSH SMB backends). WebDAV connection identified single base URL rather host/port, since URL commonly carries server-specific path prefix (per-user DAV root, instance). Supports full netfs API except SSH-permission/ownership/timestamp/symlink operations; file_move() copy followed deleting source (native rename exposed) - atomic, failed delete leaves copies behind rather neither. Two real defects underlying webdav package found worked around, confirmed live local WebDAV server: error handling inconsistent functions (throw failure, others warn return FALSE/NULL, now handled uniformly), directory listing always discards first result row assumption ’s queried collection’s entry - true directory, silently drops plain file’s entry , making file empty directory indistinguishable listing either directly; specific path’s type instead always resolved listing parent. Fixed dir_ls()/dir_info() WebDAV producing garbage paths (scheme host embedded bogus leading path segments) servers. RFC 4918 permits PROPFIND response’s <href> either server-relative path full absolute URL, server’s choice; confirmed live local WsgiDAV server uses former Hit’s .NET WebDAV Server (webdavserver.net) uses latter. now handled. Also fixed webdav() never actually checking webdav package installed (check function existed nothing called - smb() already called equivalent check, webdav() didn’t), applied construction-time check new s3() connection . Added fifth remote backend, s3(), delegating s3fs package (built paws alone - external binary). connection scoped one bucket, way smb() scoped one share. Every s3fs::s3_*() convenience function shares one connection process-wide (global cache s3_file_system() maintains internally), make second s3() connection silently clobber first one still use; netfs instead builds s3fs::S3FileSystem R6 object fresh per call uses methods directly, “rebuild, don’t share” approach already used FTP’s curl handles. Two real defects s3fs found worked around, confirmed live local MinIO server: file_copy()/file_move() internally decide S3--S3 copy, download, upload checking literal "s3://" prefix path - bare "bucket/key" string (format every s3fs method accepts works ) matches none three, call reports success silently nothing . file_info() specifically (uses future_lapply() internally), translated error thrown inside tryCatch() handler re-caught tryCatch()’s generic handler instead reaching caller - collapsing precise netfs_not_found/netfs_auth_error generic failure; fixed resolving outcome inside tryCatch() throwing returns. dir_delete() without recurse = TRUE refuses non-empty S3 “directory” way every backend’s plain delete , even though S3 atomic primitive - s3fs’s dir_delete() unconditionally recursive, checks listing first. AWS S3 authentication failures classify netfs_permission_error (HTTP 403), netfs_auth_error (401) - confirmed live wrong secret key comes back 403 even S3-compatible server (MinIO), matching AWS’s API convention using 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch genuine permission denials alike.
